staging:
the operator's notes, R7_common.md): hands off the body and above the desk while she speaks; elbows out so
the upper arms clear the torso and breasts by >= 3 cm; the mic is on HER LEFT, so big gestures are her RIGHT hand, or
both hands in front of her sternum (inside her shoulder line), never past her left shoulder line; her left hand alone
only small and low. The graphic panel (CAM_MCU_L shots) is on frame right = HER LEFT: a deictic to it is her right hand
across the body, open palm, chest height, stopping ~15 cm left of her sternum (under the mic head, never into it),
with her head and eyes turning ~10 deg that way and straight back to the lens.

pre.note: Already alive when the cut opens: an easy closed-mouth grin building, a small head tilt to his right (4 deg), an inhale with the shoulders rising 1 cm, hands loosely together at the sternum in front of him (fingers loosely laced, elbows out), at the bottom edge of the MCU frame, not on the desk. A small lean in from 0.4 s.

lines.text: Every day, WhatsApp moves over a hundred billion messages.

gestures.note: hands start 15 cm apart in front of his sternum, spread to shoulder width; L hand below the mic

lines.text: And almost none of them stay on its servers.

gestures.note: palm-down sweep out to his right: none
palms up, collarbone height: here it is

lines.note: CU, half a second of speech: the face carries it; the hands only enter at the bottom of the frame

lines.text: Open the app, and your phone keeps one connection open to WhatsApp.

gestures.note: a thumb tap on an imaginary phone
an open hand sets down 'one' in front of him at chest height (no finger count)
draws the line from his chest toward the panel: cross-body, chest height, stops 15 cm left of the sternum under the mic head

lines.text: On the server, each connection is its own tiny Erlang process.
One server once held two million of them.

gestures.note: an open hand sets down 'one server' (no finger count)
spread OUT at chest height (wrists at or below the collarbone), bowing forward, never up toward the face

lines.text: You hit send. Is your friend online?

gestures.note: open hand
a thumb press, crisp
palms up, a small shrug: well, is he?

lines.note: WIDE: elbows 20+ cm off the torso, hands up the whole line (the same fix as her 00:44 shot)

lines.text: Then it goes straight down their connection.

gestures.note: a flat hand slides straight forward

lines.text: If not, it waits. And once it's delivered, it's deleted.

gestures.note: palm out: it waits
a crisp wipe: gone

lines.text: Your ticks? One: the server has it.
